Hi Hannah,

Thanks for the demo last week — the team was impressed with the latency profile and the batching options. We're running through vendor options for a hosted inference provider to support a new product line. Ballpark numbers: we're looking at ~300B tokens/year in year 1 with an expected ramp to ~750B by year 2.

Before we move deeper on pricing and an MSA/commit, two firm constraints from our side:
- We need a DPA in place with standard data processing terms (no surprise data resale clauses).
- We require SOC 2 Type II evidence (redacted report or SOC 2 system description + auditor letter) before we sign on to any multi-year committed pricing.

Can you confirm whether: (a) commit pricing (per-token discounts) is contingent on those items, and (b) if so, what the minimal evidence is (redacted OK, required fields, timing)? Also, please send a draft mutual action plan so we can map procurement/legal timelines.

If it helps, I'll loop our procurement contact (Evan) once we have a clear list of gating items. Happy to schedule a 30-min call this week.

Hannah/Marcus — blocking checklist below that we typically require to enable committed pricing for hosted customers. This is the minimum set; anything marked as "required" must be complete before legal signs off on a commit discount clause.

Required items (pre-sign/enablement):
- Signed Data Processing Addendum (DPA) using our template or mutually agreed redlines. We can accept customer redlines but major deviations (data resale, broad subprocessor rights without notice) will need exec review. (Attachment: DPA-template.docx)
- SOC 2 Type II: either full report redacted for sensitive details OR: auditor attestation + system description that covers the Redwood control environment relevant to data processing. Reports must be within the last 12 months. Redactions are acceptable; examples of acceptable redaction are allowed. (Attachment: SOC2-redacted.zip)
- Completed security questionnaire for high-risk vendors (compressed answers okay for initial review). (Attachment: security-questionnaire.pdf)

Additional controls we verify (helpful but not strictly blocking):
- Encryption at rest & in transit (AES-256, TLS 1.2+), KMS integration options for customer-managed keys (if required).
- Data retention & deletion policy with a deletion SLA for customer data.
- Access control and audit logging: proof of limited admin access and regular log retention (30-90 days minimum; extended per enterprise plan).
- Incident response contact and SLA for breach notification.

Timing and application: once we have a signed DPA and acceptable SOC2 evidence, product/finance can enable the agreed committed tier and apply the discounted per-token rate prospectively from the contract effective date. Retroactive credits are considered on a case-by-case basis and require Finance approval.

If Marcus wants, I can draft the clause language for the MSA that ties discounts to the DPA/SOC2 acceptance milestone.

-Laura

Ashley/Evan — thank you for the quick turnaround. Per Laura and Mina the gating items to access our committed per-token discounts are: (1) signed DPA, and (2) SOC 2 Type II evidence (redacted report or attestation + system description). Once those are in our hands we can proceed to finalize the tiered pricing in the MSA.

Summary of the commercial proposal we attached (proposal-v3.pdf):
- Pilot: 3M tokens/month (30-day pilot) to validate integration and latency SLAs.
- Year 1 commit: 300B tokens/year mapped to our "enterprise X" tier — proposed per-token rate $0.00028, with step-downs at 500B and 750B.
- Billing: monthly usage invoices with near-real-time cost dashboards; commit true-up at quarter close.
- Discount activation: pricing band activated after DPA signature + SOC2 evidence receipt; we can discuss retroactive credits if both items are provided within 30 days of contract effective date (subject to finance sign-off).

Next steps I propose:

3) I'll set a 30-min technical checkpoint next week with Marcus and Mina to go over integration specifics and KMS/encryption options.
